svg.title: 40 chart types from microcharts, rendered by the library at word size
svg.desc: A wall of 40 chart types from the microcharts catalogue, each rendered by the library at word size from the sample data in its own documentation. Sparkline: A trend over ordered values, small enough to sit in a sentence. SparkBar: Compact bars for magnitude, or a win–loss streak of outcomes. ForecastCone: Will we land where we need to? Bullet: A measure against a target and qualitative bands. ActivityGrid: Calendar or matrix intensity: the contribution-graph shape. TrendArrow: Which way is this moving? At glyph size, before any number. StatusDot: What state is this thing in: shape and color paired, never color alone. Progress: How far along, exactly: bar plus the percent that is the datum. RugStrip: Where the raw observations actually sit: distribution without binning. MiniBar: Which category is biggest, and by roughly how much. PictogramRow: Counts a human can verify by counting: ●●●○○. Seismogram: When did things happen, and how hard: event density over time. HeatStrip: How intensity evolved, glanceably: the 1×N sibling of ActivityGrid. DotPlot: A few named values on one scale: minimum ink per comparison. Dumbbell: Where each row started and ended: hollow to filled, no legend. Slope: Who rose and who fell between two moments: crossings read instantly. MicroScatter: Are these two variables related? The relationship no other type tells. SegmentedBar: What is this made of, and in what proportions. HistogramStrip: What does the distribution look like? Mode, spread, skew in a cell. MicroBox: The p50 and spread of a metric: a five-number summary in a row. ProgressRing: How complete is this? At icon size, where a bar doesn't fit. MicroDonut: Roughly what is this made of? An honest, capped concession at icon size. Funnel: Where does the pipeline leak? Stage-to-stage conversion in a cell. Waterfall: How the deltas compose into the total: P&L in a cell. Horizon: A wide-range series folded into a slim, dense band. TallyMarks: How many, counted the way a human counts. DicePips: A small count or severity, read instantly as a die face. MoonPhase: How far through a cycle or period: readable across cultures. Hourglass: How much time is gone and how much remains, both at once. Honeycomb: How many of the available slots are taken. Constellation: When the rare events happened, and how big. TreeRings: How growth accumulated, period over period, from the centre out. CitySkyline: How groups compare on size, and how activated each is. MusicStaff: The shape of a short series, read as a melody. Thermometer: Where a value sits on a calibrated range, and how close to the goal. BalanceBeam: Which of two sides outweighs, and roughly by how much. WindBarb: Which way it's flowing and roughly how hard, in one character. WinProbWorm: Who's winning, and when did the lead flip? Waveform: The shape of a high-frequency signal, where its spikes and silences are, at word width. QuadrantDot: Where does it sit in the 2×2?
